title: Project board, project management team and project team
blurb: Define the project board, the project management team structure and the project team, and tell apart who directs, who is in the structure and who works on the project.
question: Which is accountable to the business for the success of the project and has authority to direct it within the remit set by the business?

teach.body: Formally: the project board is accountable to the business for the success of the project and has the authority to direct the project within the remit set by the business. In plain English: the board is the project's steering group. It answers upwards to the business layer and makes the key decisions, but it works inside the limits the business has set.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a leisure centre refit
teach.body: Westmere District Council is refitting a leisure centre. The board is executive Asha Patel (director of communities), senior user Rob Kerr (head of leisure services) and senior supplier Joan Hale (the building contractor's director). The PMT also includes project manager Liam Ford, two team managers, an assurance officer and a project support coordinator. Electricians and pool trainers join the project team. Reception staff at the centre will adopt new booking routines but do no project work: they are stakeholders outside the project team.

teach.text: Trap: the project management team structure has NO authority to direct the project; the project board does. And the board is accountable to the business, not to the project manager.

items: Board: accountable to the business for success; directs within the business's remit.
Board = executive + senior user(s) + senior supplier(s).
PMT structure: board, PM, team managers, assurance and support roles; no authority to direct.
Project team: everyone giving time to the project; affected people who do no project work sit outside it.

summary: You can now define the project board and its duties, list the roles in the project management team structure and explain who is in the wider project team. You can also say which group has authority to direct.

A.q: Which statement describes the project board?
options: Responsible for running the whole project day to day
Accountable for the quality of supplier products
Accountable to the business for the project's success
Responsible for providing the project mandate
A.why: The project board is accountable to the business for the success of the project and directs it within the business's remit (6.2.1).

whyNot.0: Running the project day to day is the project manager's job.
whyNot.1: Accountability for the quality of supplier products is the senior supplier's.
whyNot.3: The project mandate comes from the business layer.

A.q: Which roles make up the project board?
options: Executive, senior user and senior supplier
Executive, project manager and senior user
Senior user, senior supplier and project manager
Executive, senior supplier and project assurance
A.why: The board consists of the executive, senior user(s) and senior supplier(s).

whyNot.1: The project manager reports to the board but is not a member.
whyNot.2: The project manager is not a board member, and the executive is missing.
whyNot.3: Project assurance is carried out on behalf of the board but is not a board role; the senior user is missing.

A.q: Which is a responsibility of the project board?
options: Setting work package tolerances for teams
Providing the project mandate for start-up
Delivering products to the agreed specifications
Setting stage tolerances and the change budget
A.why: The board sets stage tolerances and the change budget to support decision-making and management by exception.

whyNot.0: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager.
whyNot.1: The project mandate comes from the business layer.
whyNot.2: Delivering products to specification is the team manager's responsibility.

B.q: Which statement about the project management team structure is correct?
options: It directs the project within the business's remit
It lists the roles but has no authority to direct
It includes the business layer and the board
It replaces the project board on small projects
B.why: The PMT structure is composed of the board, PM, team managers, assurance and support roles; it does not itself have authority to direct the project (6.2.3).

whyNot.0: Directing within the business's remit is the project board's authority.
whyNot.2: The business layer is outside the project management team.
whyNot.3: A board is needed on every project; tailoring may combine roles but keeps the board.

B.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. The project board has authority to direct the project.
2. The project board is accountable to the project manager.
3. Board members are part of the project team.
4. The business layer is part of the project management team.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: The board directs the project (1), and board members such as the senior user are inside the project team (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: the board is accountable to the business; the PM reports to the board.
whyNot.1: Both are false: the board answers to the business, and the business layer is outside the PMT.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the business layer sits outside the project management team.

B.q: A department manager will adopt the project's new process in her area but does no project work. How is she best described?
options: A stakeholder outside the project team
A member of the project board
A member of the project management team
A team manager at the delivering level
B.why: People within the business who are affected by the project but do not work in the project team can still contribute, for example by integrating new products into their area.

whyNot.1: Board members hold a directing role; she has no role in the project.
whyNot.2: The PMT holds management roles; she is affected but holds none.
whyNot.3: Team managers deliver work packages; she does no project work.

C.q: Who is the project board accountable to, and within what does it direct the project?
options: The executive; the stage tolerances it sets
The project manager; the project plan
The business; the work package tolerances
The business; the remit set by the business
C.why: The board is accountable to the business and directs the project within the remit the business has set.

whyNot.0: The executive is part of the board; the board as a whole answers to the business.
whyNot.1: The project manager reports to the board, not the other way round.
whyNot.2: Work package tolerances are set by the PM for teams; the board works within project tolerances.

C.q: Which group has authority to direct the project, and which simply sets out the management roles?
options: PMT structure; project board
Project board; PMT structure
Project team; project board
Business layer; project team
C.why: The project board directs; the project management team structure describes the roles and has no authority to direct.

whyNot.0: This is reversed: the board directs and the PMT structure sets out the roles.
whyNot.2: The project team has no authority to direct.
whyNot.3: The business layer sets the remit but the board directs the project within it.

C.q: Which is a PRINCE2 7 project board duty concerning people?
options: Setting tolerances for individual team members
Allocating work packages to the team managers
Supporting social cohesion and team well-being
Carrying out day-to-day management of teams
C.why: The board focuses on the safety and well-being of the project team and monitors and supports social cohesion in the project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: Team managers set tolerances for their team members.
whyNot.1: The project manager authorizes work packages for team managers.
whyNot.3: Day-to-day management is done by the project manager and team managers.

reteach.title: A film: producers, crew list and everyone on set
reteach.question: On a film, who decides, who is on the management list, and who is actually working on set?

blocks.body: The producers decide and answer to the studio (project board). The credits list the management roles: producers, director, heads of department, script supervisor (PMT structure), but a list cannot make decisions. Everyone on set, from camera operators to extras, is the wider crew (project team). The cinema staff who will show the film are affected but do not work on it.

blocks.text: Only the board directs. The PMT structure is the set of roles and has no authority of its own.

explain.body: The project board is accountable to the business for the project's success and directs it within the remit set by the business.

test.q: Who is the project board accountable to?
options: The project manager
The business
The senior user
The team managers
test.why: The board is accountable to the business for the project's success.

whyNot.0: The project manager reports to the board.
whyNot.2: The senior user is a member of the board.
whyNot.3: Team managers report to the project manager.

explain.body: One executive, plus one or more senior users and one or more senior suppliers.

test.q: How many executives can a project board have?
options: Two
One per interest
As many as needed
One
test.why: There cannot be more than one executive.

whyNot.0: Sharing the executive role between two people is not allowed.
whyNot.1: The executive represents the business interest; users and suppliers have their own roles.
whyNot.2: Several people are allowed for senior user and senior supplier, not executive.

explain.body: The project management team structure is composed of the project board, project manager, team managers, project assurance and project support roles. It does not itself have authority to direct.

test.q: Which roles are in the project management team structure?
options: Board, PM, team managers, assurance and support
Business layer, board, PM and team managers
Business layer, board and project assurance
PM, team managers, team members and users
test.why: The PMT structure is the board, PM, team managers, project assurance and project support roles.

whyNot.1: The business layer is outside the PMT.
whyNot.2: The business layer is outside the PMT, and the PM is missing.
whyNot.3: The board is missing, and users without a role are not in the PMT.

explain.body: The project team covers everyone who gives their time to the project. People affected by the project who do not work in it are stakeholders outside the project team.

test.q: Which person is outside the project team?
options: A senior user who sits on the project board
A team manager delivering one work package
A user adopting products who does no project work
A specialist who works part-time on one product
test.why: People affected by the project who do not work within the project team sit outside it.

whyNot.0: Board members, including the senior user, are inside the project team.
whyNot.1: Team managers are inside the project team.
whyNot.3: Anyone giving time to project work, part-time or not, is in the project team.
